contract: Whether Cal.com's own branding is suppressed must be resolved for the *event* being booked, through the single org-aware resolver in `packages/features/profile/lib/hideBranding.ts` (`shouldHideBrandingForEvent` / `shouldHideBrandingForTeamEvent` / `shouldHideBrandingForUserEvent` / `getHideBranding`), which folds the parent organization's `hideBranding` over the team's or the user's own column. Every consumer — the public booking/confirmation pages the attendee sees AND the workflow/automation reminder pipeline that emails or texts them — must obtain the flag from that resolver (and must select `team.parent.hideBranding` / the owner's org profile in the underlying query), so that an attendee-facing automated message and the booking page for the same event agree. Reading a raw `hideBranding` column straight off `eventType.owner`, `booking.user` or `eventType.team` breaks the contract, because the organization-level override is silently dropped and paying org customers keep seeing vendor branding.

defect_location.summary: The canonical, org-aware rule lives in packages/features/profile/lib/hideBranding.ts:35-45 (`resolveHideBranding` returns true whenever the organization has branding hidden) and is exposed via packages/features/profile/lib/hideBranding.ts:50-80 and :85-181. The booking-page side obeys it: apps/web/server/lib/[user]/[type]/getServerSideProps.ts:299, apps/web/lib/team/[slug]/[type]/getServerSideProps.tsx:199, apps/web/app/(booking-page-wrapper)/team/[slug]/[type]/pageWithCachedData.tsx:36, apps/web/lib/d/[link]/[slug]/getServerSideProps.tsx:61,103, apps/web/lib/org/[orgSlug]/instant-meeting/team/[slug]/[type]/getServerSideProps.ts:85, apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-single-view.getServerSideProps.tsx:253 and packages/features/ee/payments/pages/payment.tsx:58 all call the resolver. The automation side does not. Every workflow-scheduling call site passes the owner's raw column instead: packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:2618,2793,2808, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleConfirmation.ts:459,472, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:471, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleBookingRequested.ts:112, packages/features/handleMarkNoShow.ts:377, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:561, packages/app-store/_utils/payments/handlePaymentSuccess.ts:230, packages/features/ee/round-robin/roundRobinManualReassignment.ts:671 and packages/features/ee/managed-event-types/reassignment/services/ManagedEventManualReassignmentService.ts:188 all use `!!eventType(.owner)?.hideBranding` — no team, no parent organization. The cron send path repeats the mistake in its own vocabulary at packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:246-248, 274-276 and 433-435 (`eventType?.team?.hideBranding : booking.user?.hideBranding`), fed by the query shape in packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/getWorkflowReminders.ts:40, 170, 197-203, which selects only `team.parentId`/`team.hideBranding` and `user.hideBranding` and never the parent org's flag. The flag then travels untouched through packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/reminderScheduler.ts:56,97,161,213,248,262-284, packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/scheduleMandatoryReminder.ts:18-82 and packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:38,115,147,182,204 into packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/service/EmailWorkflowService.ts:229-233,244,487-492, which renders the branded template. EmailWorkflowService.ts:90-93 and WorkflowService.ts:133-136 do call `getHideBranding`, but keyed on the *workflow's* userId/teamId rather than the booked event's owner/team, so they too can disagree with the booking page.
